sources.title: Miyachi, Dipper’s hypothesis and self-injective endomorphism rings
sources.date_version: OWR17/2009, workshop22–28March2009; contribution printed944–947; DOI10.4171/OWR/2009/17. Whole report publication23December2009 in Crossref.
sources.read_scope: Contribution physical28–31, printed944–947; repeated actual body29–31 especially §0.3 Thm5 and §0.4 Conj7/Remark8.
sources.comparison: Stable-rank FI(λ) convention and unit parameter q; Conj7 proposes projectivity at some n≥length, then a stronger index-set bridge. Thm5 concerns self-injectivity of endomorphism rings, a different condition. Characteristic zero is assumed only in subsequent §0.5. No later correction/restriction found in this bounded route.

sources.title: De Visscher–Donkin, On projective and injective polynomial modules
sources.date_version: Institutional manuscript12January2005, cover warns unspecified version; MathZ251(2005)333–358, DOI10.1007/s00209-005-0805-x; Crossref online31May2005, printOctober2005.
sources.read_scope: Physical1–7 plus8,11–14,16,19–22,25–28,36 (printed pages one less after cover). §2.4, Lemmas3.1–3.3, Thm4.1, Conj5.1/5.2, conditionalThm5.1, Cor6.1, §7 and Prop7.3/Cor7.2.
sources.comparison: Established costandard reciprocity, projective-injective/tilting equivalence, labelled truncation and symmetric-power decomposition are old ingredients. Conj5.1 assumes I(λ) projective and predicts an infinitesimal/column-regular alternative. General q=1 positive characteristic is admitted; §7 uses characteristic zero after the reduction. This classification is distinct from Miyachi’s simple-top bridge and is not refuted by nonprojective I(λ).
sources.gap: Manuscript not proved byte-identical to journalVOR; remaining pages not read exhaustively. No unconditional use of conditionalThm5.1.

sources.title: Donkin–Geranios, Injective Schur Modules
sources.date_version: arXiv1704.02416v1,8April2017, internal16March2017; journal online23April2017, JAlgebra484(15August2017)109–125, DOI10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.04.007 (York metadata).
sources.read_scope: Actual printed5–7 and15–17: Prop1.3.1, Remark2.22, Definition3.1, Prop3.2, Remark3.3, Example3.4.
sources.comparison: Prop1.3.1 gives stable Schur-functor identifications. Prop3.2 relates injective partitions (∇=I) to Specht modules that are Young, with converse when quantum characteristic≥3. This does not say I is projective. Example3.4 is characteristic2 and not the target characteristic3 all-rank obstruction.
sources.gap: Other pages not exhaustively read; do not infer complete absence from term scan.

sources.title: Donkin–Geranios, Endomorphism Algebras of Some Modules for Schur Algebras and Representation Dimension
sources.date_version: Actual cover11February2013; York early online24March2013; AlgebrasRepTheory17(2),April2014,623–642, DOI10.1007/s10468-013-9412-4; arXiv1704.02409v1 uploaded8April2017.
sources.read_scope: Printed1–3,9–11, especially Lemma3.6, Remark3.7, Prop3.8, Cor3.9 and Lemma4.1.
sources.comparison: Constructs polynomial injectives and symmetric endomorphism algebras for representation-dimension bounds. Remark3.7 explicitly describes consistency with DDConj5.1. These inspected statements neither assert nor refute the full simple-top/existential-rank bridge. Self-injective or symmetric End(I) does not mean I projective.
sources.gap: 2017 body is a repost; journalVOR not compared byte-for-byte. Unread sections remain.

sources.title: Donkin–Geranios, Polynomially and Infinitesimally Injective Modules
sources.date_version: Actual manuscript cover11May2013; JAlgebra392(15October2013)125–141, DOI10.1016/j.jalgebra.2013.05.033; arXiv1704.02405v1 repost8April2017.
sources.read_scope: Printed1–2,12–13,18; Theorem4.1 and the continuation of Prop5.3/rank-two explicit criterion.
sources.comparison: Theorem4.1 decides injectivity after restriction to the first infinitesimal subgroup using divisibility index; rank two is made explicit. Infinitesimal injectivity is a different predicate from polynomial projectivity. These statements alone are not a full bridge counterexample.
sources.gap: Other sections and journalVOR not exhaustively compared.

sources.title: Fang–Miyachi, Hochschild cohomology and dominant dimension

sources.title: Fang–Wei Hu–Koenig, Dominant and global dimension of blocks of quantised Schur algebras
sources.date_version: Corrected2021 VOR; online22June2021, MathZ300(2022)463–473, DOI10.1007/s00209-021-02792-w. Publisher notes correction22August2021.
sources.comparison: Computes global/dominant dimensions of blocks with stable rank n≥r. It explicitly distinguishes n<r, which is not treated. This is not a projectivity criterion for individual polynomial injectives over every allowed rank.
sources.gap: Remaining sections not exhaustively read; Wei Hu is distinct from Jun Hu in S13-gap.

sources.title: Erdmann–Law, Torsion pairs and Ringel duality for Schur algebras
sources.date_version: arXiv2104.05317v1,12April2021; body matched peer's independently recorded SHA. Read only after authorized peer challenge.
sources.comparison: Published nonsplit rank-two sequences specialize at p3 and weight difference3, with determinant restored, to the local degree-five obstruction. Its simplicity criterion handles difference5. Combined with old DD structural facts, the all-rank obstruction is a short synthesis. This strengthens derivative-component credit; it does not establish that the full bridge refutation was already printed.
